18.1.intro: The right tools depend on your stage. Buying tools too early slows your site and drains cash.

steps.say: Decide your stage: day one (just starting), stage 1 (steady sales every week) or stage 2 (several channels and real ad spend).
steps.check: You know which column of the lesson's table is yours.

steps.say: For each need in the table, compare what you use now with the tip for your stage.
steps.check: You have a list of gaps, and of tools you don't need yet.
steps.lost: Check just your email tool against the table.

steps.say: Cancel tools that are ahead of your stage. Add only the one gap that matters most.
steps.lost: Cancel one tool you don't need yet.

18.2.intro: Every app costs money and speed. Four steps make sure each one earns its spot.

steps.say: Name the number the tool should improve. Example: "email sign-ups per 100 visitors".
steps.check: The tool has a target number.
steps.lost: Write one number it should move.

steps.say: Check its monthly cost as a share of sales, and how much it slows your site.
Try it for a set time, like 30 days.
steps.check: The trial has an end date in your calendar.
steps.lost: Put the end date in your calendar.

steps.say: Remove it if the number didn't get better.
steps.check: Only tools that move a number stay.
